items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: I was lucky enough to play behind Aretha Franklin once in the saxophone section

ctx.x: Not so much John because at that point John was one of the respected tenor players of the day, not the icon that he later became. I certainly liked his playing in some ways I want to say that I liked his earlier playing better than some of his later music for a number of reasons that I have explored a lot in the book that I’m writing, how the music changed and what different things influenced it. Billie Holiday I certainly knew how revered she was and that was — was that a year earlier? I can’t remember if that…

I related to that immediately because I was lucky enough to play behind Aretha Franklin once in the saxophone section, and I found that within the first five minutes that I had to stop paying attention to her because I wasn’t covering my part.
